subject: Capacity planning: Dedicated GPU pool for Galileo Health - terms & sizing
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@galileohealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning: Dedicated GPU pool for Galileo Health - terms & sizing

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a proposed starting point for a Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool and align on the tradeoffs you mentioned (latency vs cost, peak bursts during EOD processing). Below are the inputs we have from Galileo and the sizing questions we need answered to finalize a formal quote: 

- Current steady-state request rate: ~180 reqs/min for embeddings endpoint, 25 reqs/min for chat/generation during business hours (08:00–18:00 PT).
- Peak bursts: up to 6x steady-state for ~30 minutes overnight for batch ingest (approx midnight PT).
- Typical prompt sizes: 1–2k tokens for chat; some analytics jobs up to 8k context.
- Target P95 latency for chat generation: <= 600ms.
- Concurrency requirement: 120 concurrent short-chat sessions; batch jobs can be queued.

Open questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the 8k-context jobs are batched and tolerate queueing (yes/no + desired SLA for batch completion)?
2) Do you expect sustained 6x bursts daily or just spikey weekly runs?
3) Any regulatory/region restrictions that would force on-prem or VPC-only deployments?

If the inputs above look right, Rishi and I can run a quick capacity model and send a short pricing options table (monthly reserved commits and a couple discount tiers).

Next steps I propose: quick 30-min call Thursday to confirm the batch SLA and concurrency distribution so we can finalize the quote.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: galileo-workload-snapshot.csv (CSV export of recent traffic), sample SLA matrix

Subject: Re: Capacity planning: Dedicated GPU pool for Galileo Health - terms & sizing

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 8k context jobs are primarily nightly analytics (ML feature extraction). They can be queued; completion within 2 hours is acceptable for most jobs, but a subset (~10%) needs <30 minute turnaround.
- Peak bursts are daily but vary; the EOD processing you saw is fairly consistent M-F with occasional weekend pressure.
- No on-prem constraints yet; we prefer VPC in us-west for data locality.

Procurement looped in — they typically ask for 12-month and 24-month committed pricing options, with an option to scale up mid-term. Also curious if you offer a usage offset if we go with an initial smaller commit and then add on over the first quarter.

Happy to do the 30-min call Thursday 11:00 PT.

Best,
Asha Menon
Head of ML Platform | Galileo Health
asha@galileohealth.com

Hi all — quick sizing notes based on Monica's snapshot and Asha's clarifications. Kept it conservative to hit your P95 target and the 10% low-latency subset for nightly jobs.

Assumptions used:
- Chat workload: average generation length ~1.2k tokens; P95 requirement = 600ms.
- Embeddings workload: small models, high QPS (~180 reqs/min).
- Nightly analytics: 8k context, ~10% need <30m completion window.
- Baseline GPU profile: A100-class equivalent (we can map to specific instance SKUs in the contract).

Recommended GPU pool (starting):
- 6x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated with auto-burst queue capacity to maintain sub-600ms for chat at 120 concurrent sessions. This supports steady-state plus 2x headroom for typical daytime spikes.
- For nightly EOD 6x bursts, enable scheduled autoscale to add 8 GPUs for a 2-hour window (burst credits billed at reserved rate + burst premium) — alternatively, purchase a slightly larger reserve (12 GPUs) for smoother economics if you want no burst premiums.

Pricing/commit options (ballpark for discussion):
- 12-month commit: base rate $X per GPU / month (redacted here) with 18% discount off list.
- 24-month commit: base rate with 26% discount and priority capacity SLA.
- Start-small option: 6 GPU commit for 3 months at 12% introductory discount, then convert to 12/24-month at full commit discount with credit for months already paid (usage offset up to 40% of first quarter spend).

Risks & notes:
- If the 8k jobs shift to more strict latency needs, we recommend separating them onto a small high-memory GPU group to avoid contention.
- Quantization/FP16 can reduce cost by ~20% on generation workload but requires validation for quality-sensitive prompts.

If this looks reasonable, Monica can draft a formal quote with the two commit tiers and a clause for mid-term scale-up credits. Also happy to provide a quick cost-per-request model showing expected $/1k requests for each commit size.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Asha / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick answers and for joining the call yesterday. Per our conversation and Rishi's sizing, attached is a short, formal quote (Galileo-Quote-May2027.pdf) and the workload snapshot you asked for. Summary of the proposal and next steps: 

Summary (proposal):
- Starter reserved pool: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs, 12-month commit, 18% discount. Includes scheduled autoscale for nightly window up to +8 GPUs (burst premium applies).
- Growth reserve: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs, 24-month commit, 26% discount, includes priority capacity SLA and 2 scaling credits per year for mid-term growth.
- Start-small path: 3-month pilot at 6 GPUs with 12% discount and crediting of first-quarter spend up to 40% when converted to full commit.

Commercial notes:
- We can provide a PO-ready quote and DocuSign link if procurement confirms the desired commit term (12 vs 24 months) and preferred billing cadence.
- If you want to avoid burst premiums entirely, choose the 12-GPU reserved option; otherwise the scheduled autoscale keeps upfront costs lower.

Action items:
1) Procurement: please confirm preferred commit length and whether Galileo requires a line-item for burst premium in the SOW.
2) Galileo ML Platform: confirm whether the 10% subset of nightly jobs truly needs <30 minute turnaround (helps decide whether to isolate on separate GPUs).
3) Redwood: we'll produce a PO-ready quote and a cost-per-request breakdown by Friday EOD.

If there are follow-ups, we can loop in legal for standard SLA language. Proposed next meeting: May 24 at 11:00 PT to sign off on commit length and finalize SOW.

Thanks,
